samples.summary: Test "a forged `infra` key cannot suppress a finding" passes for the wrong reason and asserts the opposite of the contract
samples.evidence: The fixture at prior-findings.test.mjs:507-514 carries `infra: true` AND `lane: "backlog"`. In `carryForwardFindings` the `f.lane !== "backlog"` filter (prior-findings.mjs:159) runs before the projection, so the record is dropped by the lane rule; the assertion `deepEqual(..., [])` at line 516 holds whether or not the `infra` ordering fix exists. The inline comment ("It is dropped as an infra record only because of the forged key") is therefore false, and the test's title/assertion directly contradict the sibling test at line 528-537, which asserts the same forged-`infra` shape IS carried. As written this test would keep passing if the infra filter were moved back before the projection — i.e. it provides zero coverage of the very regression it is presented as guarding — and it documents the suppression behaviour as desired, inviting a future "fix" that reinstates the bug.

samples.summary: The round bound is now ENFORCED (refusal) and `--force` overrides it, but no test exercises either code path
samples.evidence: `cmdReview` gained `if (notice && !args.force) return fail(notice)` / `console.warn(... --force ...)` at spec-to-pr.mjs:886-888 — a behavioural change from the previous advisory warning. The only tests under the header "the bound is enforced, with one explicit override" (spec-to-pr.test.mjs:155-162 and 659-666) assert string content of `roundBoundNotice` alone; neither runs the CLI. The refusal is trivially testable end to end (`review --round 4 --dry-run --out <base>` hits the bound check before the dry-run return), and `--force` proceeding is equally reachable. If the guard regressed — e.g. `args.force` truthiness or the `notice &&` condition — a non-converging loop would keep spending panel rounds with nothing failing.
searchedFor: read all CLI-driving tests in spec-to-pr.test.mjs (execFileSync blocks)

samples.summary: The carry-forward projection's evidence-bearing fields (line, evidence, claimType, searchedFor, mergedFrom, adjudication) are never asserted
samples.evidence: `carryForwardFindings` projects an explicit field list (prior-findings.mjs:166-179), and the module comment states the local projection deliberately keeps evidence the cloud trims. Every test in prior-findings.test.mjs:441-542 uses fixtures with only `severity`/`file`/`summary`, so a typo or removal in any of the other projected keys — including `line`, which the new terminal reporter prints as `file:line`, and `evidence`, which the next round's verifier reads — would silently drop that data with the suite still green. The tests do cover that unknown keys are dropped, but not that wanted keys survive.

samples.summary: `blockingFindingsIn` (verdict-on-disk → terminal report wiring) is unexported and untested
samples.evidence: `blockingFindingsIn` at spec-to-pr.mjs:791-800 reads `<outDir>/<lens>/verdict.json` and feeds `renderBlockingFindings`. `renderBlockingFindings` is tested on hand-built fixtures (spec-to-pr.test.mjs:164-203) and `carryForwardFindings` on verdict fixtures, but nothing covers this join — the same class of 'both ends tested, wiring not' gap the diff's own comment on `prepareRoundInputs` (spec-to-pr.mjs:620-628) says three rounds kept raising. A wrong path join here yields an empty report while the run still exits 1, so the developer sees lens ids and no findings.

samples.summary: The dry-run carry-forward report line (`[dry-run] carrying N prior finding(s)`) has no test
samples.evidence: spec-to-pr.mjs:898 and 912 compute and print prior findings under `--dry-run`. The two CLI dry-run tests (spec-to-pr.test.mjs:358-374 and the `--fresh` one at ~430-455) only ever exercise round 1 or a freshly-reset base, where `round > 1` is false, so the `priorFindingsFor` branch of the dry run is never executed. A dry run that under-reports (or crashes on) the carry-forward would answer the one question this mode exists to answer wrongly, and the suite would not notice.

samples.summary: The real (non-dry-run) `--fresh` deletion loop in `cmdReview` is untested
samples.evidence: spec-to-pr.mjs:867-871 deletes `round-*` directories on a real run. Coverage is limited to the pure `roundDirsToClear` helper (spec-to-pr.test.mjs:216-222) and the dry-run test asserting nothing is deleted. Nothing asserts the real run actually clears the rounds, nor that it clears only them under a hostile `--out`; the destructive half of the behaviour (the one whose earlier version deleted whatever `--out` named) has no end-to-end guard. It is reachable in a test: `--fresh` with an invalid `--rebuttals` path deletes first and then fails before any git/network work.

samples.summary: Only the leaf branch of the directory guard is covered end to end; the ancestor walk and symlink-leaf refusals are fixture-only
samples.evidence: The CLI test at spec-to-pr.test.mjs:~500-524 stages a 0755 leaf and asserts the refusal. `unsafeBaseReason` is unit-tested for symlink/ancestor cases with hand-built stat objects (lines 227-244, 636-655), but the ancestor loop at spec-to-pr.mjs:855-862 — including the `realpathSync` resolution and the `ownedPathChain` boundary choice — is never run against a real filesystem, so a wiring error there (e.g. passing the leaf instead of its dirname, or the wrong `leaf` flag) would not be caught.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo. The fixture at prior-findings.test.mjs:507-514 carries both `infra: true` and `lane: "backlog"`, and prior-findings.mjs:159 applies `.filter((f) => f.lane !== "backlog")` BEFORE the projection (166-179) and before the infra filter (192). The record is therefore dropped by the lane rule, so the `deepEqual(..., [])` at line 516 holds whether the infra filter sits before or after the projection — the assertion is insensitive to the very ordering fix its comment claims to demonstrate. The inline comment at line 515 ("dropped as an infra record only because of the forged key") is false, and it contradicts the sibling test at 534-537, which asserts the same forged `infra: true` shape (without `lane`) IS carried. The second half of the test (519-525) uses an `honest` fixture with no `infra` key, so it covers projection key-stripping, not the infra ordering. carryForwardFindings is new in this diff (absent from .trusted/scripts/agent/prior-findings.mjs), so this is newly added, self-contradicting coverage. The sibling test at 528-542 does guard the ordering regression, which contains the blast radius, but it does not make the test at 501 non-vacuous — no refutation ground applies to the vacuous assertion and false rationale themselves.
